shortcut_explanation: 99 is 1 less than 100. So 99 + 99 is 2 less than 200.
full_explanation: 99 + 99 is the same as 100 + 100 take away 2. That is 198, which is less than 200. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Give both fractions the same bottom number. 2/3 = 10/15 and 3/5 = 9/15.
full_explanation: Multiply the top and bottom of 2/3 by 5 to get 10/15. Multiply the top and bottom of 3/5 by 3 to get 9/15. 10 fifteenths is more than 9 fifteenths. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: 0.25 is 25 hundredths. A quarter of 100 is 25.
full_explanation: 1/4 means 1 ÷ 4. Think of 1 as 100 hundredths: a quarter of 100 hundredths is 25 hundredths, which is 0.25. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: 10% means divide by 10. 250 ÷ 10 = 25.
full_explanation: 10% is one tenth. One tenth of 250 is 250 ÷ 10 = 25. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

quantity_b: \text{the area of a square with side } 5
shortcut_explanation: Area is length times width. 3 × 8 = 24, and 5 × 5 = 25.
full_explanation: The rectangle covers 3 × 8 = 24 squares. The square covers 5 × 5 = 25 squares. 25 is more than 24. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Evenly spaced numbers balance around their middle. The middle of 10 and 40 is 25.
full_explanation: Pair them up: 10 with 40, and 20 with 30. Each pair has an average of 25. That means the average of all four is 25. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.
3³ means three 3s multiplied: 3 × 3 = 9, and 9 × 3 = 27. 5² means 5 × 5 = 25. 27 is more than 25. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Without brackets, do × and ÷ from left to right. So A is 3 × 3 = 9, but B is 12 ÷ 12 = 1.
full_explanation: In A, work from the left: 12 ÷ 4 = 3, then 3 × 3 = 9. In B, the brackets go first: 4 × 3 = 12, then 12 ÷ 12 = 1. 9 is more than 1. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: 0 times itself is always 0. Any number (except 0) to the power 0 is 1.
full_explanation: 0⁵ = 0 × 0 × 0 × 0 × 0 = 0. 5⁰ = 1, because each time the power goes down by 1 you divide by 5: 5² = 25, 5¹ = 5, 5⁰ = 1. 1 is more than 0. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Dividing by a quarter asks how many quarters fit in a half: 2. Multiplying by a quarter takes a quarter of a half: 1/8.
full_explanation: Two quarters make a half, so ½ ÷ ¼ = 2. A quarter of a half is ⅛, so ½ × ¼ = ⅛. 2 is much more than ⅛. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: 0.9 + 0.09 = 0.99. That is 1 hundredth short of 1.
full_explanation: 0.9 is 90 hundredths and 0.09 is 9 hundredths. Together they make 99 hundredths, which is 0.99, a little less than 1. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: √0.25 is 0.5, because 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25. The root of a number between 0 and 1 is bigger than the number.
full_explanation: 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25, so √0.25 = 0.5. 0.5 is more than 0.25. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Work from the inside out. |−4| is 4, and the minus sign outside makes it −4.
full_explanation: |−4| = 4, because −4 is 4 steps from 0. Then the minus sign in front turns 4 into −4. Both quantities are −4. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: Always test 0. x = 1 makes 3x bigger, but x = 0 makes both 0.
full_explanation: If x = 1, then 3x = 3 and 2x = 2, so A is bigger. If x = 0, both are 0, so they are equal. (A negative x would even make B bigger.) So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: Half of a half is a quarter. So A is a quarter of 80 and B is half of 80.
full_explanation: 50% of 80 is 40. 50% of that 40 is 20. 20 is less than 40. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Odd times odd is always odd. An odd number leaves 1 when you divide by 2.
full_explanation: 15 and 17 are both odd, so 15 × 17 is odd too: it is 255. Any odd number divided by 2 leaves a remainder of 1. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

condition: \text{a bag of } 30 \text{ marbles has red and blue marbles in the ratio } 2 : 3
shortcut_explanation: Red is 2 parts out of 2 + 3 = 5 parts. 2 out of 5 is less than half.
full_explanation: The 30 marbles split into 5 equal parts of 6. Red is 2 parts: 12 marbles. Half of all the marbles is 15. 12 is less than 15. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Adding a number smaller than the average pulls the average down. 2 is far below the average of 4 and 9.
full_explanation: The average of 4 and 9 is 13 ÷ 2 = 6.5. Adding the 2 gives 15 for three numbers, and 15 ÷ 3 = 5. 5 is less than 6.5. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: A square is never negative, but x is negative here. Try x = −3: x² = 9.
full_explanation: For any negative x, x² is a negative times a negative, which is positive. A positive number is always more than a negative one. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Between 0 and 1, the root is bigger than the number. Try x = ¼: √¼ = ½.
full_explanation: For x between 0 and 1, √x × √x = x, and multiplying by a number less than 1 makes things smaller. So x must be smaller than √x. With x = ¼, √x = ½, which is bigger. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Try x = ½: 1/x = 2. Dividing 1 by a number less than 1 gives more than 1.
full_explanation: 1/x asks how many x's fit into 1. If x is less than 1, more than one fits, so 1/x is more than 1. And x itself is less than 1. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: x and −x are the same distance from 0, just on opposite sides. Try x = 3: |3| = 3 and |−3| = 3.
full_explanation: |x| is how far x is from 0. −x is the mirror image of x across 0, so it is just as far away. That is true for a positive x, a negative x and 0. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: x ≤ 0 lets x be 0. Try x = 0 (equal) and x = −1 (B is bigger).
full_explanation: If x = 0, then x + 5 = 5, so they are equal. If x = −1, then x + 5 = 4, which is less than 5. So the answer is D: not enough information.

quantity_a: \text{the remainder when } n + 1 \text{ is divided by } 2
shortcut_explanation: It depends on whether n is even or odd. Try n = 2, then n = 3.
full_explanation: If n = 2, then n + 1 = 3, which leaves 1 when divided by 2: equal. If n = 3, then n + 1 = 4, which leaves 0: B is bigger. So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: x% of 200 is the same as 200% of x, which is 2x. Doubling a positive number makes it bigger.
full_explanation: x% of 200 means x hundredths of 200, which is 2 × x. Since x is positive, 2x is more than x. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: y is 6 more than x. The average sits halfway, so it is 3 more than x.
full_explanation: The average of x and y is (x + x + 6) ÷ 2 = (2x + 6) ÷ 2 = x + 3. That is exactly Quantity B. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: Open the brackets: 2x + 6 and 3x + 6. Both have + 6, so compare 2x with 3x.
full_explanation: 2(x + 3) = 2x + 6 and 3(x + 2) = 3x + 6. If x = 1, that is 8 and 9, so B wins. If x = −1, it is 4 and 3, so A wins. So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: 3 + 1 = 4 equal parts make 20, so each part is 5. x is 3 parts: 15.
full_explanation: The ratio 3 : 1 splits 20 into 4 equal parts of 5. x gets 3 of them, so x = 15. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

quantity_a: \text{the perimeter of a square with side } s
shortcut_explanation: Don't compare perimeter and area by feel. A side of 2 gives 8 and 4, but a side of 5 gives 20 and 25.
full_explanation: The perimeter is 4 × s and the area is s × s. If s = 2: 8 and 4, so A wins. If s = 5: 20 and 25, so B wins. So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: The third side can be anything between 2 − 2 = 0 and 2 + 2 = 4. Try 1 and 3.
full_explanation: Two sides of 2 can make a third side longer than 0 and shorter than 4. If x = 1, B is bigger. If x = 3, A is bigger. So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: 99 lots of n is 100 lots of n, take away one n.
full_explanation: 100 × n − n means 100 n's with one taken away, which leaves 99 n's. That is exactly 99 × n, for any number n. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: Try x = −2: x³ = −8, which is further below 0 than −2. Cubing a number below −1 makes it more negative.
full_explanation: If x is less than −1, x² is more than 1. x³ = x² × x, and multiplying x by a number bigger than 1 moves it further from 0. x is negative, so it moves further down: −8 is less than −2. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: √(x²) is the size of x without its sign. For a negative x, that is −x.
full_explanation: Try x = −5: √((−5)²) = √25 = 5, and −x = −(−5) = 5. For any negative x, −x is positive and is exactly the size of x. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: Try x = 2 and y = 3. y/x = 3/2 is more than 1, but x/y = 2/3 is less than 1.
full_explanation: Because 0 < x < y, the bigger number y is on top in A, so y/x is more than 1. In B the smaller number is on top, so x/y is less than 1. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Try a big number and then 0. x = 2 makes them equal, but x = 0 gives 1 and −1.
full_explanation: If x = 2: |2 − 1| = 1 and |2| − 1 = 1, so they are equal. If x = 0: |0 − 1| = 1, but |0| − 1 = −1, so A is bigger. So the answer is D: not enough information.

quantity_b: p \text{ after a } 20\% \text{ and then a } 5\% \text{ discount}
shortcut_explanation: Two discounts don't simply add up. The 5% is taken from a price that is already lower, so it takes off less.
full_explanation: Try p = 100. A takes off 25, leaving 75. B takes off 20, leaving 80, then 5% of 80, which is 4, leaving 76. 76 is more than 75. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

quantity_a: \text{the average of } a, b \text{ and } c
shortcut_explanation: a + c is two b's, so a + b + c is three b's. Three b's shared by 3 is b.
full_explanation: a + b + c = (a + c) + b = 2b + b = 3b. Divide by 3 for the average: b. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

quantity_a: \text{the remainder when } n \text{ is divided by } 3
condition: n = 3k + 5 \text{ and } k \text{ is an integer}
shortcut_explanation: Split 5 into 3 + 2. Then n is a multiple of 3, plus 2.
full_explanation: n = 3k + 5 = 3k + 3 + 2 = 3(k + 1) + 2. The 3(k + 1) part divides by 3 exactly, so 2 is left over. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: (a + b)² is a² + b² plus an extra 2ab. Here a and b have different signs, so 2ab is negative.
full_explanation: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b². With a positive and b negative, ab is negative, so the extra 2ab makes B smaller than a² + b². So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: You don't need to find x and y. x − y = 2 is positive, so x is bigger.
full_explanation: x − y = 2 means x is 2 more than y. (If you want the numbers: x = 6 and y = 4.) So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

quantity_a: \text{the perimeter of a rectangle with area } 36
shortcut_explanation: Don't assume it is a square. A 6 by 6 square has perimeter 24, but a 4 by 9 rectangle has perimeter 26.
full_explanation: A 6 by 6 rectangle has area 36 and perimeter 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24, which is equal. A 4 by 9 rectangle also has area 36, but perimeter 4 + 9 + 4 + 9 = 26. So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: × 1.1 pushes a number away from 0, and ÷ 1.1 pulls it closer. Which is bigger depends on the sign.
full_explanation: If x = 10: 10 × 1.1 = 11 and 10 ÷ 1.1 is about 9.1, so A wins. If x = −10: −11 and about −9.1, so B wins. So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: x² < 1 means x is between −1 and 1. Try ½, then try −½.
full_explanation: If x = ½: x⁵ = 1/32 and x³ = ⅛, so B is bigger. If x = −½: x⁵ = −1/32 and x³ = −⅛, and −1/32 is closer to 0, so A is bigger. So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: Square both to compare. (x + 3)² is x² + 9 plus an extra 6x.
full_explanation: Both quantities are positive. B squared is x² + 6x + 9, and A squared is x² + 9. Since x is positive, 6x is positive, so B is bigger. Try x = 4: √25 = 5, but 4 + 3 = 7. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

quantity_a: \text{the remainder when } m + n \text{ is divided by } 2
condition: m \text{ and } n \text{ are integers, and } mn \text{ is odd}
shortcut_explanation: A product is odd only when both numbers are odd. Odd plus odd is even.
full_explanation: If m or n were even, mn would be even. So both are odd. Two odd numbers add up to an even number, and an even number leaves 0 when divided by 2. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: Flipping a fraction can flip the order, but not always. Try a = 2, b = 1, then a = 1, b = −1.
full_explanation: If a = 2 and b = 1: 1/a = ½ and 1/b = 1, so B wins. If a = 1 and b = −1: 1/a = 1 and 1/b = −1, so A wins. So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: A square only cares about distance from 0. A bigger square means further from 0.
full_explanation: a² is |a| × |a| and b² is |b| × |b|. If a² is bigger than b², then |a| must be bigger than |b|. Try a = −5, b = 3: 25 > 9, and 5 > 3. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

quantity_b: \text{the average of } x, y \text{ and } z
shortcut_explanation: z is bigger than both x and y, so it is bigger than their average. Adding it pulls the average up.
full_explanation: The average of x and y is somewhere between them, so it is less than z. Adding a number above the average always raises it. Try x = 2, y = 4 and z = 9: the average goes up from 3 to 5. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

quantity_a: p \text{ after an } x\% \text{ rise and then an } x\% \text{ fall}
shortcut_explanation: The fall is taken from a bigger number than the rise was. So you always end below where you started.
full_explanation: Try p = 100 and x = 10: a 10% rise makes 110, and a 10% fall takes away 11, leaving 99. The same happens for any x: the fall is x% of a bigger number. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

condition: \text{a triangle has sides } x, 5 \text{ and } 8, \text{ and } x \text{ is an integer}
shortcut_explanation: The third side must be more than 8 − 5 = 3. A whole number more than 3 is at least 4.
full_explanation: In a triangle, 5 + x must be more than 8, so x is more than 3. Since x is a whole number, the smallest it can be is 4, which is more than 3.5. If x could be a fraction, it could be 3.2, but it can't. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.
